correctness.rationale: The three switch cases are exhaustive for 2 <= m <= n except C4. An automorphism interchanging the swapped endpoints yields exact vertexwise equality of all refinement colours by induction. Detours and exterior arc embeddings (Kuratowski for 2x4) prove connected planarity. The length-three-path argument yields a precisely signed four-cycle-count difference +2 at (3,3), -2 elsewhere. C4 is the unique simple degree-two graph on four vertices. The supplied checker reproduced each assertion in 152 grids of sides at most 18; the all-size proof is explicit and does not rely on the finite check.

value.rationale: This constructs a uniformly short, geometry-preserving counterexample to C2 identification for every genuinely two-dimensional rectangular grid, even when the competitor is required to remain connected and planar. Prescribing the minimal two-edge exchange and exact four-cycle difference gives a precise structural obstruction to detecting planar square-cell information; the sole C4 exception and the 3x3 sign reversal locate sharp boundaries. The motivation is not an arbitrary finite parameter choice but a natural graph family and restricted planar definability question.
